overrides_applied.source: Form 10-K for fiscal year ended December 31, 2025 (filed 2026-02-11, accession 0000913144-26-000012), Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows (p. F-8): the investing-activities section lists only fixed-maturity / short-term / equity / other investment flows, derivatives settlements, investments in other ventures and the Validus purchase — there is no purchases-of-property-and-equipment (or any capex) line for FY2025, FY2024 or FY2023, and the Consolidated Balance Sheets (p. F-5) carry no property-and-equipment line. The statement fully reconciles without one: FY2025 operating $3,693,107 thousand + investing $(2,215,809) thousand + financing $(1,410,503) thousand + FX $(12,218) thousand = the reported net increase in cash of $54,577 thousand exactly; FY2024: $4,164,822 - $3,060,856 - $1,287,515 - $17,365 = reported $(200,914) thousand exactly; FY2023: $1,911,634 - $3,822,636 + $2,588,639 + $5,542 = reported $683,179 thousand exactly. EDGAR companyfacts for CIK 913144 contains no capex fact under any candidate tag in any year.
overrides_applied.reason: DATA_GAP:capex — capex missing for FY2023, FY2024, FY2025 (and every other year) because the filer does not report a capex line at all; the filer's own cash-flow statements fully account for investing activities in all three years, so capex is $0 as a filing fact, not an estimate (same presentation as the EG/CMPS precedents). Any premises/equipment spend is aggregated inside the filed investing lines and is immaterial at insurer scale — even a hypothetical $50M would move OE by ~$1.08/share (~1.4% of the $77.78 base). The engine's history already carried capex as assumed-zero, so the override changes no OE figure; it converts a silent zero-fill into a sourced, registered decision.

fragility_flags: STALE_FY: latest fiscal year ended 10 months ago — check TTM/quarterly OE and consider --base-oe-ps override
BASIS_BREAK_SUSPECT: a >60% revenue jump/drop in the last 5 yrs — check for divestitures, big M&A, or restatements before trusting any CAGR
OE_VOLATILE: OE/share range over the last 5 yrs spans >3x — normalized base helps but the business is cyclical; widen bear weight
NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE: net income and operating cash flow differ by >40% in 2024 — find the one-off (tax deposits, impairments, WC swings) before trusting the OE base
SECTOR_MODEL_MISMATCH: Finance sector — OE/capex DCF fits finance names poorly; grade confidence low

override_impact.basis: engine-native normalized base (median of last 3 FY) and weighted IRR, DCF run both ways (zero-fill baseline vs with-override); a --base-oe-ps TTM base is excluded from both sides — its override effect shows in ttm.py output
